# Soṇa Sutta (Ud 5.6 (PTS Ud 57))

**ID:** Ud 5.6 (PTS Ud 57)
**Section:** Udāna (ud)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Soṇa Sutta
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0503m.mul4.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Soṇa Sutta* (Ud 5.6; PTS Ud 57) recounts the story of the monk Soṇa Koṭikaṇṇa (or Kuṭikaṇṇa), a young man residing in the remote western region of Avanti who is only able to obtain higher ordination after protracted delays due to the scarcity of bhikkhus in the border country [Fronsdal 2016; Levman 2014]. Having trained under Mahā Kaccāna, Soṇa undertakes a journey to meet the Buddha and stays overnight in the Buddha's own dwelling [Fronsdal 2016; Levman 2014]. Towards dawn, invited by the Buddha to speak or recite the Dhamma, Soṇa chants all sixteen poems of the *Aṭṭhakavagga* (found in the *Sutta Nipāta*) with clear intonation and delivery, earning the Buddha's high praise and formal approval (*abbhanumodi*) [Fronsdal 2016; Levman 2014; Garfield and Westerhoff 2015; O'Neill 2016].

Scholars consider this discourse a crucial benchmark for the history and transmission of early Buddhist literature [Fronsdal 2016; Levman 2014]. It provides direct canonical testimony that the *Aṭṭhakavagga* already existed as an independent, organized sixteen-poem collection at an extremely early stage [Fronsdal 2016; Levman 2014]. The narrative also illustrates the reliance on memorized metric poetry for preserving and disseminating Buddhist doctrine, as well as the importance attached to proper chanting diction and phonetic fidelity [Fronsdal 2016; Levman 2014; Garfield and Westerhoff 2015]. Furthermore, the episode is studied as an early canonical precedent for internal cross-referencing and textual recitation within Buddhist scriptural traditions [Levman 2014; O'Neill 2016].

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Passage-level parallels: UV 28 Pāpavarga; T 212.29 ◎惡行品第二十九; T 213.28 法集要頌經罪障品第二十八; Uv Kg 28 Sin; UVS 28 Pāpavarga; Kd 5 Cammakkhandhaka
- Mentioned in: snp4.1-16

**Sources**

- [Fronsdal 2016] Gil Fronsdal, Buddha before Buddhism: Wisdom from the Early Teachings (2016) — Discussed Soṇa's discipleship under Mahā Kaccāna in Avanti and the sutta's testimony to the early existence of the Aṭṭhakavagga.
- [Levman 2014] Bryan Geoffrey Levman, Linguistic Ambiguities, the Transmissional Process, and the Earliest Recoverable Language of Buddhism (2014) — Analyzed Soṇa's overnight stay with the Buddha, verbatim recitation of the Aṭṭhakavagga, and transmission in Vinaya collections.
- [Garfield and Westerhoff 2015] Jay L. Garfield and Jan Westerhoff, Madhyamaka and Yogacara: Allies or Rivals? (2015) — Noted the Buddha's approval of Soṇa reciting the verses with proper intonation.
- [O'Neill 2016] Colin O'Neill, Self-Referential Passages in Mahāyāna Sūtra Literature — Examined the sutta as an example of early canonical references to distinct subsections of discourses.
